fills.notes: The phrase must name the three receptacles into which the elements are poured; the following clause “which he had established…” requires a plural antecedent. Likely “pits … which,” with the remaining visible letter w beginning “which.”

fills.fill: and when he had poured them in,
fills.notes: After the construction of the worlds, the narrative needs a temporal/causal hinge leading to the residue (“something remained behind…”). A neutral procedural clause fits the oldest impersonal register.
Introduces the consequential remainder on the earth’s surface; keeps the correspondential logic: containment is never total in ultimates, hence a ‘remainder/mark’ persists.
The context lists volcanic mountains/islands and then shifts to sterile regions (“places where no fruit sprouts”). A third natural correspondent of fire’s residue is arid/burnt ground.
Bridges from the volcanic ‘fumes of fire’ to the next sign (sterility).

fills.fill: there is no heat ... there is no moisture
fills.notes: The lacuna sits between ‘limb’ (i.e., extremity/border) and ‘trees shall not bear fruit’; the correspondential cause of barrenness is lack of the two generatives in nature—heat and moisture—here withdrawn by the dominance of the fiery remnant.
The sentence demands what was removed from the firmaments: the upper ‘waste/poison’ is explicitly water. The genitive ‘of the rulers’ matches the preceding ‘poison of the rulers who are above.’
Darkness is ‘swept out’ and then ‘shut…in that ___ of darkness’; the same cosmological pattern as the water-vessel in ¶9 implies a containing vessel for darkness before the boundary with water.

Requires a boundary relation between the imprisoned darkness and the sea: darkness is enclosed in its vessel ‘as a wall’ set over/against the water, preserving discrete regions (sea-wall vs. darkness-wall) in the cosmos’ circumference.
The clause needs a simple conjunction: “he discharged the fire … and at that time again…”

The firmaments are purified ‘as a place for the light-givers to journey’; the missing parallel is the prepared ‘road/path’ (ordered traverse) in the cleansed region—an impersonal functional term suited to the substrate.

Completes the procedural sequence: sweeping out the three impurities results in fixed orderly ascent/paths for the three powers before the Porter; “courses” matches the cosmological-register of regulated movement.

assessment: Most gaps can be constrained by the text’s repeated threefold procedure (discharge → draw up like-to-like → sweep out → contain as vessel/wall → leave a natural ‘mark’). Exact phrasing in ¶6 and the boundary description in ¶10 remains tentative because the surviving context gives function more clearly than specific wording.
